primitives.name: Market Probability from Moneylines
primitives.verbatim_quote: Market probability = proportional de-vig of the two closing moneylines; ties excluded.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'m': 'moneyline value (dimensionless)', '\\Delta m': 'difference between home and away moneylines (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Moneylines are symmetrically distributed around zero; ties are excluded from probability calculation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When moneylines approach ±1000, convergence to extreme probabilities occurs.

layer2.mapping: Market probability maps directly to GSI's calibrated belief distribution through reliability curve alignment.
layer2.telemetry: Reliability curve slope deviation from unity indicates calibration quality.

primitives.name: Isotonic Calibration Validation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Post-isotonic ECE per fold (equal-width/adaptive): worst folds 2021 (0.0888/0.0391) and 2023 (0.0859/0.0112); the equal-width number is inflated by sparse tail bins — the adaptive binner is the honest one.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\bar{p}_b': 'average predicted probability in bin b (dimensionless)', '\\bar{y}_b': 'average actual outcome in bin b (dimensionless)', 'n_b': 'number of samples in bin b (count)', 'N': 'total number of samples (count)'}
primitives.assumptions: Bins must be ordered such that increasing probability implies increasing accuracy; adaptive binning avoids sparsity artifacts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Sparse tail bins cause inflated ECE estimates in equal-width schemes.

layer2.mapping: Adaptive binning enables robust estimation of isotonic calibration error; used in GSE to validate model consistency.

primitives.name: Murphy Decomposition Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: The Murphy decomposition here is computed on 10 equal-width bins, so it carries a finite-bin (within-bin) residual of ≈0.033; the Brier is exact.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\text{Brier}': 'quadratic loss function (dimensionless)', '\\text{Reliability}': 'deviation from perfect calibration (dimensionless)', '\\text{Resolution}': 'ability to distinguish classes (dimensionless)', '\\text{Uncertainty}': 'entropy of true class distribution (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Equal-width bins introduce finite-bin residuals; exact Brier requires infinite granularity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Finite-bin approximation introduces systematic bias in reliability estimation.

layer2.mapping: Murphy decomposition underpins GSI's reliability diagnostics; informs GSE's adaptive calibration thresholds.
layer2.telemetry: Residual term quantifies binning-induced noise in reliability metrics.
